solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cop's latest action when manoeuvring US car

indicators.note: the latest letter of the cop is the final one of that word
manoeuvring moves things about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police officer's most recent move is to steer an American automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' takes P, the last letter of 'Cop'; 'when manoeuvring' rearranges ACTION into ONTIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiac was a General Motors brand of automobile sold in America.

clue.text: One who goes down the pit, continually striking?

definitions.text: One who goes down the pit, continually striking?

parts.words: One who goes down the pit, continually striking?
parts.note: the pit reads like a coal mine with miners on strike, but it is the orchestra pit, home of the player of drums and cymbals

explanation.surface: A coal miner who keeps walking out on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchestra pit is where theatre musicians play.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer or timpanist plays instruments by hitting them, in the orchestra pit.

clue.text: Sign of approval in France where bucket emptied? Yes

parts.note: a nod of the head shows approval
ou is French for where

indicators.note: emptied removes the contents, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: A French nod of agreement over an emptied bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' leaves BT from bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: No doubt is used as an affirming phrase, certainly, as an equivalent of yes.

clue.text: This writer meets butcher somewhere in the Hebrides

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
to butcher is to slaughter or slay

explanation.surface: The writer meets a butcher on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famed for whisky.

clue.text: Pencil ruined historical pictures shown here

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: ex means former, from history

explanation.surface: A broken pencil spoils old drawings on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges PENCIL into CINEPL. 'pictures' looks like drawings but means films.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineplex is a multi-screen cinema where films, the pictures, are shown.

clue.text: Home left in springtime, on the whole

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Overall, someone was at home and left alone during the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainly and on the whole are synonyms meaning for the most part, generally.

clue.text: Islamist mostly consumes English breakfast item?

indicators.note: consumes takes something in, so a letter goes inside
mostly means not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Islamist here loosely means a Muslim

explanation.surface: A Muslim eats a full English breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MUSLIM to MUSLI; 'consumes' puts E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and fruit, eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Corner of room Nigel plastered certainly not satisfactory

indicators.note: plastered means drunk, so the name's letters reel about

parts.note: no is a firm refusal
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: Nigel decorated a corner of the room, and the plasterwork is not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' rearranges NIGEL into INGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inglenook is a recess beside a large open fireplace, a cosy nook.

clue.text: Acted as guide around globe and, as expected, spotted animal

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the others

parts.note: led means guided
O is globe-shaped
par means the normal or expected level

explanation.surface: A tour guide circled the world and, sure enough, saw a wild cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a big cat famous for its spotted coat.

clue.text: Smell wine Noel circulated at church

parts.note: red is a type of wine

indicators.note: circulated suggests moving round, so the name's letters are shuffled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Noel passed a bottle of wine round at church, and it smelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' rearranges NOEL into OLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolence is a strong pleasant odour or fragrance, a literary word for a scent.

clue.text: Obese informer having heart transplant?

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is swapped for another, like a heart being replaced

parts.note: a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: An overweight police informant undergoes heart surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having heart transplant' swaps the central A of GRASS for an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can describe someone extremely fat, a dated sense of the word for very large.

clue.text: Elaine ran with Rose when abroad in West Africa

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or widely scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elaine went running with Rose on an overseas holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when abroad' rearranges ELAINE RAN ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sierra Leonean is a native of Sierra Leone, a country of West Africa.

clue.text: Occasionally suss out and track financial offence

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is picked

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Investigate occasionally and pursue a crime involving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes alternate letters of 'suss out', giving USU.
explanation.definitionFit: Usury is lending money at extortionate interest, historically an illegal practice.

clue.text: Greek character, long-term convict, not one to decline crime

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: not signals that a piece is left out of the convict's word

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence
I is the Roman numeral one
to age is to decline with years

explanation.surface: A Greek lifer who refuses to go into decline turns to crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one' removes I from LIFER, leaving LFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilferage is petty theft, the stealing of small items, which is a crime.

clue.text: Nice neighbour with case of Shiraz welcoming guy on Times

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other pieces go inside
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: T is time, so TT stands for times
a guy is a rope used to steady a tent

explanation.surface: Someone from a city near Nice brings Shiraz and greets a chap reading the Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective. 'welcoming' puts the other pieces inside the case of Shiraz; two Ts stand for times, one per time.
explanation.definitionFit: St Tropez is a Riviera resort a short distance along the coast from Nice.

clue.text: Changeable writer dying to probe dictionary

indicators.note: to probe means to go into, so the pieces sit inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a pen is a writing instrument
end means death, dying

explanation.surface: A volatile author, close to death, studies a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to probe' means going inside the dictionary, which splits around the writer and the dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-ended means having no fixed limit, so open to adjustment.

clue.text: Potter's trick, rebounding snooker ball onto specific part of table

definitions.note: Potter's reads as potter is: the definition is the verb, to move about aimlessly

indicators.note: the ball's word is attached after the table marking

parts.note: a do is a swindle or trick
the D is a marked semicircle on a snooker table

indicators.note: rebounding sends the ball back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a red is a snooker ball

explanation.surface: A snooker player's trick shot: a ball bouncing back into the D.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebounding' turns RED into DER. 'Potter' looks like a snooker player but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to totter or potter about unsteadily, like an elderly person.

clue.text: Female fashion designer keeps a drawer for measuring device

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so pieces go inside

parts.note: Mary Quant was a British designer who popularised the miniskirt
DR is a banking abbreviation for drawer, debtor

explanation.surface: A woman designer keeps a chest of drawers for her tape measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like a furniture drawer but is the banking abbreviation DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is an instrument for measuring angles, used in navigation.

clue.text: A world of great opportunity maybe in cowboy's territory?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Cowboy country may offer a whole world of opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'the world is your oyster'; 'maybe' marks it as an example and 'in' signals the answer lies inside 'cowboy's territory'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says the world is your oyster when life offers every opportunity.

clue.text: I needed to house student who pays the bill

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the setter of the puzzle refers to themself as I
L is a learner, a student

explanation.surface: I had to put up a student who covers the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter, so it gives SETTER rather than the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is someone who settles an account or debt, paying what is owed.

clue.text: Correspondence Irishman recalled on boat

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Liam is a common Irish man's name

explanation.surface: A letter from an Irishman remembered while aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns LIAM into MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unsolicited advertising post, a kind of correspondence.

clue.text: Perhaps this means travelling on A1 the wrong way?

definitions.text: Perhaps this means travelling on A1 the wrong way?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it
travelling means moving about, so the letters are rearranged
the wrong way means backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A1 read as A and 1, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Losing one's memory may lead to driving north up a major road against the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges MEANS into AMNES; 'the wrong way' turns AI into IA. The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is memory loss, which might make one forget which way to go.

clue.text: At the periphery, the brothers served up dessert

indicators.note: served up in a down clue reads upwards, so the letters go backwards
the periphery means the edge, so only the outer letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: Siblings on the sidelines brought out a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the periphery' takes TE from 'the'; 'served up' turns TE plus BROS into SORBET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a frozen water ice flavoured with fruit, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Another loony seen in papers causing obstruction

indicators.note: seen in places the jumble inside the papers

parts.note: ID means identity papers

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A second lunatic is spotted in the newspapers, blocking things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' gives NTHEROA, a jumble of the word Another, which 'seen in' places inside the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the road is in the way, physically or figuratively obstructing progress.

clue.text: Horse secure before event's final round

indicators.note: the fastening word comes before the remaining pieces

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or secure

indicators.note: the final letter of the word event is wanted

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Fasten a horse before the last round of a showjumping event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' takes T, the last letter of 'event'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse with patches of white.

clue.text: Leaf picker, the ultimate electronic gadget

parts.note: a leaf of a book is a page

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last

explanation.surface: A tea-leaf picker uses the latest electronic device.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a small radio device that beeps to alert its wearer to messages.

clue.text: Like some roofs westwards, it had lead

indicators.note: in an across clue westwards means right to left, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: led means had the lead, was in front

explanation.surface: A roof facing west had been made of lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'westwards' reads 'it' backwards. 'lead' suggests the roofing metal but means was in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Many roofs are covered in overlapping clay or slate tiles.

clue.text: Adventure novel mentioned weapon for shooting game

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: a bow is a weapon for shooting arrows, and a jest is a game or bit of fun

explanation.surface: A spoken tale of firearms for hunting game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW JEST said out loud gives the novel's title. 'game' looks like hunted birds but means a jest.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Geste is P. C. Wren's 1924 novel of the French Foreign Legion.

clue.text: Central characters in secret pledge united faith

indicators.note: the central characters are the middle two letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: At the heart of a secret pledge lies shared faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central characters in' takes CR from secret, ED from pledge and IT from united.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means belief or trust, as in giving credit to a story.

clue.text: Turtle avoiding soft ground

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
p is piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A turtle steers clear of soft earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding soft' removes P from TERRAPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features.
